question: Who among the following is the world renowned exponent of the bamboo flute?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hariprasad Chaurasia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is the world-renowned exponent of the bansuri (bamboo flute), celebrated for popularising it as a leading concert instrument of Hindustani classical music. (बांसुरी — हरिप्रसाद चौरसिया)

 

• He trained in vocal music under Pandit Rajaram Paramar and later learned the bansuri and Hindustani classical music from Annapurna Devi.

 

• He is a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan (2000), and formed the famous 'Shiv-Hari' duo with santoor maestro Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, composing music for several Bollywood films.

 

• He has performed extensively worldwide and is widely credited with elevating the bansuri from a folk instrument to a major classical solo instrument.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The bansuri is a side-blown transverse flute made of bamboo, traditionally associated with Lord Krishna in Indian iconography.

 

NOTE

 

• MS Subbulakshmi (Option 1): A legendary Carnatic vocalist, the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna; not associated with the flute.

 

• Ravi Shankar (Option 2): World-renowned sitar maestro, not a flautist.

 

• Bismillah Khan (Option 4): Legendary shehnai player, recipient of the Bharat Ratna; the shehnai is a distinct reed instrument, not a bamboo flute.

question: What is net investment?
option_1: Sum of all the investments in a country
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross investment - depreciation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Net Investment = Gross Investment − Depreciation (Capital Consumption Allowance). (निवल निवेश — सकल निवेश घटा मूल्यह्रास)

 

• Gross investment is the total expenditure on capital goods (machinery, buildings, equipment) in an economy during a period, including spending that merely replaces worn-out capital.

 

• Depreciation represents the wear and tear/consumption of existing capital assets during production.

 

• Net investment reflects the actual addition made to an economy's productive capital stock after accounting for depreciation; it can even be negative if depreciation exceeds gross investment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Net investment is a key determinant of an economy's long-run growth in productive capacity, distinct from gross investment which also includes replacement investment.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Simply summing all investments does not account for depreciation and is not the definition of net investment.

 

• Option 2: Adding depreciation to gross investment overstates capital formation; this is not a recognised economic concept.

 

• Option 3: Subtracting indirect taxes from gross capital investment is unrelated to the concept of depreciation-adjusted net investment.

question: India won the ICC Men Cricket World Cup for the first time in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1983.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its first ICC Men's Cricket World Cup (then the Prudential Cup) in 1983, defeating the two-time defending champions West Indies in the final at Lord's, London. (क्रिकेट विश्व कप 1983 — भारत की पहली जीत)

 

• The Indian team was captained by Kapil Dev, whose all-round performances (including a famous 175* against Zimbabwe in the same tournament) were pivotal to the campaign.

 

• This victory is widely regarded as a turning point that popularised cricket across India.

 

• India went on to win the ODI World Cup for a second time in 2011, again as hosts, under the captaincy of MS Dhoni.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1983 World Cup was only the third edition of the tournament and the first not to be won by the West Indies.

 

• India also won the inaugural ICC T20 World Cup in 2007 under MS Dhoni's captaincy.

 

NOTE

 

• 1996 (Option 1): The World Cup was co-hosted by India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka; Sri Lanka won the title.

 

• 1992 (Option 2): Held in Australia and New Zealand; Pakistan won the title.

 

• 1987 (Option 3): The Reliance Cup, co-hosted by India and Pakistan; Australia won the title.

question:
Match the following institutes with their respective founders of British India.

Institutes

a. Asiatic Society of Bengal

b. Sanskrit College of Benaras

c. Fort William College

d. Calcutta Madrasa

Their respective founders

i. Warren Hastings

ii. Lord Wellesley

iii. Jonathan Duncan

iv. Sir William Jones
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded in 1784 in Calcutta by the Orientalist scholar and judge Sir William Jones, to promote the study of Asian history, culture and science. (एशियाटिक सोसाइटी ऑफ बंगाल — सर विलियम जोंस)

 

• The Sanskrit College of Benaras was founded in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan, then the British Resident at Benares, to preserve and promote Hindu law, philosophy and Sanskrit learning.

 

• The Fort William College was founded in 1800 in Calcutta by Governor-General Lord Wellesley, primarily to train young British civil servants in Indian languages and administration.

 

• The Calcutta Madrasa was founded in 1781 by Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of India, for the study of Persian and Arabic (Islamic law).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• These institutions mark the early phase of Orientalist scholarship and colonial education policy in British India, before the shift towards English education after Macaulay's Minute of 1835.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 pair the institutes with incorrect founders; only the combination a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i matches the historically correct founder for each institute.

question: Kathakali, one of the classical dances of India, is predominantly performed in which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form that originated in and is predominantly performed in Kerala. (कथकली — केरल)

 

• It combines dance, drama, music, and elaborate costumes, headgear and facial makeup (vesham) to depict stories from the Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas.

 

• Communication is through stylised hand gestures (mudras), facial expressions (navarasas) and eye movements rather than spoken dialogue.

 

• It is traditionally accompanied by instruments such as the chenda, maddalam, chengila and vocal narration (sopanam style).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala is also home to other classical/traditional performing arts such as Mohiniyattam, Koodiyattam (a UNESCO-recognised Sanskrit theatre form) and Theyyam (a ritual dance form).

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Home to the classical dance form Sattriya.

 

• Manipur (Option 2): Home to the classical dance form Manipuri.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Associated with the classical dance form Kathak, not Kathakali.

question: Identify the oldest iron and steel company of India from the following options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tata Iron & Steel Company(TISCO).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established in 1907 by Jamsetji Tata at Sakchi, which later grew into the city of Jamshedpur (Jharkhand); it is the oldest and first integrated iron & steel company in India among the given options. (टाटा आयरन एंड स्टील कंपनी — भारत की सबसे पुरानी इस्पात कंपनी)

 

• Commercial steel production at TISCO began in 1912; the company was renamed Tata Steel in 2005.

 

• The Indian Iron & Steel Company (IISCO) was set up later, in 1918, at Burnpur, West Bengal.

 

• The Mysore Iron & Steel Works was established in 1923 at Bhadravati, Karnataka, and was subsequently renamed the Visvesvaraya Iron & Steel Works in 1962 — so Options 2 and 4 refer to the same company at two different points in its history, and both are younger than TISCO.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The very first iron works in India, the Bengal Iron Works (Kulti, 1874), predates TISCO but is not among the given options.

 

NOTE

 

• Visvesvaraiya Iron & Steel Works (Option 2) and Mysore Iron & Steel Works (Option 4): Both refer to the Bhadravati plant established in 1923, making it younger than TISCO (1907).

 

• Indian Iron & Steel Company (Option 3): Established in 1918, also younger than TISCO.

question: The magnificent Kailasa temple at Ellora was built during the reign of which Rashtrakuta king?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishna I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kailasa (Kailasanatha) Temple, Cave 16 at Ellora, was built in the 8th century CE under the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I. (कैलाश मंदिर, एलोरा — कृष्ण प्रथम, राष्ट्रकूट वंश)

 

• It is the largest monolithic rock-cut structure in the world, carved vertically downwards from the top of a single basalt hill rather than tunnelled horizontally, so the entire temple complex is a single continuous piece of rock.

 

• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is designed to represent Mount Kailasa, his mythical abode.

 

• The Ellora caves, in Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) district of Maharashtra, comprise 34 caves — Buddhist, Hindu and Jain — and were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Krishna I's reign (c. 756-773 CE) is considered a high point of Rashtrakuta architectural patronage.

 

• Ajanta (Buddhist paintings) and Ellora (rock-cut sculpture of three faiths) were both inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1983.

 

NOTE

 

• Indra III (Option 2): A later Rashtrakuta king (early 10th century CE), known for his military campaigns including a raid on Kannauj.

 

• Govinda III (Option 3): A powerful Rashtrakuta ruler (c. 793-814 CE), known for extensive military conquests, not for building the Kailasa temple.

 

• Amoghavarsha (Option 4): A Rashtrakuta king (successor of Govinda III) known for his long, largely peaceful reign and for authoring the Kannada work Kavirajamarga.

question: In which state/UT is the Hemis festival celebrated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ladakh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hemis Festival is celebrated at the Hemis Monastery in Ladakh, commemorating the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche). (हेमिस महोत्सव — लद्दाख)

 

• It is held annually in June/July according to the Tibetan lunar calendar and features masked Cham dances performed by monks depicting the victory of good over evil.

 

• Hemis Monastery, belonging to the Drukpa lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, is the largest and wealthiest monastery in Ladakh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Ladakh include the Losar (Ladakhi New Year) and the Ladakh Festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Known for festivals such as Baisakhi and Hola Mohalla, not Hemis.

 

• Sikkim (Option 2): Known for festivals such as Losar and Saga Dawa, not Hemis.

 

• Lakshadweep (Option 3): Not associated with the Hemis Festival, which is specific to Ladakh's Buddhist monasteries.

question: Which of the following is the largest artificial lake of Asia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhopal Lake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Upper Lake of Bhopal (Bhojtal), built in the 11th century by the Parmara king Raja Bhoj, is regarded as the largest man-made/artificial lake in Asia. (भोपाल की भोज झील — एशिया की सबसे बड़ी कृत्रिम झील)

 

• It was created by constructing an earthen dam across the Kolans River, and today forms part of the Bhoj Wetland, a designated Ramsar site.

 

• The lake is a major source of drinking water for Bhopal city, earning it the nickname "the City of Lakes."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lower Lake of Bhopal, a smaller lake, lies adjacent to the Upper Lake and together they form the twin lakes of Bhopal.

 

NOTE

 

• Naini Lake (Option 1): A natural freshwater lake in Nainital, Uttarakhand.

 

• Dal Lake (Option 3): A natural lake in Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir, famous for its houseboats and floating gardens.

 

• Chilika Lake (Option 4): A natural brackish-water lagoon in Odisha, the largest coastal lagoon in India and second largest in the world, but not artificial.

question: In 2002, Zakir Hussain became the youngest percussionist to be honoured with which award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Bhushan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Legendary tabla maestro Ustad Zakir Hussain was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2002, becoming the youngest percussionist to receive this honour at the time. (ज़ाकिर हुसैन — पद्म भूषण, 2002)

 

• He had earlier received the Padma Shri in 1988, and went on to receive the Padma Vibhushan in 2023.

 

• He is also internationally acclaimed, having won Grammy Awards for albums such as 'Planet Drum' (1992) alongside Mickey Hart, and further Grammys in later years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Zakir Hussain is the son of the renowned tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha and is widely credited with popularising the tabla on the global stage through collaborations across genres.

 

NOTE

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Option 1): Zakir Hussain received this national performing-arts honour in 1990, before his 2002 Padma Bhushan.

 

• Grammy Award (Option 2): He won his first Grammy in 1992, a separate honour from the 2002 Padma Bhushan referenced in the question.

 

• National Heritage Fellowship (Option 4): A US National Endowment for the Arts honour that Zakir Hussain received in 1999, not in 2002.

question: Microbes like Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are used for:
solution_text:
The correct answer is nitrogen cycling.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are all bacteria central to the nitrogen cycle. (राइजोबियम, नाइट्रोसोमोनास, नाइट्रोबैक्टर — नाइट्रोजन चक्र)

 

• Rhizobium lives symbiotically in the root nodules of leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen (N2) into usable ammonia (biological nitrogen fixation).

 

• Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia into nitrite, and Nitrobacter further oxidises nitrite into nitrate — together carrying out nitrification, a key step of the nitrogen cycle.

 

• These processes convert atmospheric/organic nitrogen into forms plants can absorb, sustaining soil fertility and the broader ecosystem's nitrogen balance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Denitrifying bacteria such as Pseudomonas denitrificans convert nitrates back into atmospheric nitrogen, completing the nitrogen cycle.

 

NOTE

 

• Carbon cycling (Option 2): Driven by processes like photosynthesis, respiration and decomposition, not by these specific bacteria.

 

• Water cycling (Option 3): Driven by physical processes such as evaporation, condensation and precipitation.

 

• Sulphur cycling (Option 4): Involves different microbes, such as Thiobacillus, not Rhizobium/Nitrosomonas/Nitrobacter.

question: With reference to Sepoy Mutiny of 1857, on which of the following dates did the soldiers at Meerut start their journey to Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10 May.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Revolt of 1857 broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857, when sepoys rebelled against their officers over the greased cartridges issue and then set off towards Delhi, reaching it the next morning. (1857 का विद्रोह — मेरठ, 10 मई)

 

• On reaching Delhi, the rebel sepoys proclaimed the aged Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar II as their symbolic leader.

 

• The immediate trigger for the uprising was the introduction of the new Enfield rifle, whose cartridges were rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat, offending both Hindu and Muslim sepoys.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• An earlier spark of unrest occurred at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857, when sepoy Mangal Pandey attacked his British officers, an event often seen as a precursor to the Meerut outbreak.

 

NOTE

 

• 19 April, 2 June and 29 March (Options 2, 3 and 4): None of these correspond to the date the Meerut sepoys began their march to Delhi; 29 March is instead associated with the Mangal Pandey incident at Barrackpore.

question: Who among the following was selected as the Sherpa for India’s G20 hosted in 2022-23?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amitabh Kant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Amitabh Kant, former CEO of NITI Aayog, was appointed India's G20 Sherpa for India's G20 Presidency (2022-23). (अमिताभ कांत — भारत के G20 शेरपा)

 

• As Sherpa, he represented India in G20 negotiations and coordinated the agenda leading up to the G20 Summit held in New Delhi in September 2023.

 

• A 'Sherpa' is the personal representative of a head of state/government who prepares the ground for international summits such as the G20 and G7.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's G20 Presidency ran from 1 December 2022 to 30 November 2023, under the theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (One Earth, One Family, One Future).

 

NOTE

 

• Piyush Goyal (Option 1): Union Minister for Commerce & Industry, not the G20 Sherpa.

 

• Ashwini Vaishnav (Option 2): Union Minister for Railways, Communications and IT, not the G20 Sherpa.

 

• Shaktikanta Das (Option 3): Served as Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, not as India's G20 Sherpa.

question: Purvanchal Himalayas does NOT comprise of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pir Panjal range.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Purvanchal (Eastern) Himalayas/Hills comprise the Patkai Bum, Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, Mizo (Lushai) Hills and the Barail Range, extending south from the eastern Himalayan syntaxis along India's north-eastern border. (पूर्वांचल पहाड़ियां — नागा, मणिपुर, मिज़ो पहाड़ियां)

 

• These hills are formed by the same tectonic folding that created the Himalayas but run in a broadly north-south direction, are lower in elevation, and are densely forested.

 

• The Pir Panjal Range, by contrast, lies in Jammu & Kashmir/Himachal Pradesh and is part of the Lesser (Middle) Himalayas, entirely unrelated to the Purvanchal system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pir Panjal Range separates the Kashmir Valley from the Chenab basin and contains passes such as the Pir Panjal Pass and Banihal Pass.

 

NOTE

 

• Naga hills, Manipur hills and Mizo hills (Options 1, 3 and 4): All are genuine components of the Purvanchal Himalayas in India's north-east.

question: In which year did India make its Olympic debut in hockey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India made its Olympic hockey debut at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, and won the gold medal, the first of eight Olympic hockey golds for India. (भारत हॉकी ओलंपिक पदार्पण — 1928, एम्स्टर्डम)

 

• The team was captained by Jaipal Singh Munda, while Dhyan Chand emerged as the tournament's standout performer and India's top scorer.

 

• Hockey was not held as an Olympic event at the 1924 Paris Olympics, so India had no opportunity to compete in hockey before 1928.

 

• India went on to win six consecutive Olympic hockey gold medals from 1928 to 1956.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dhyan Chand, often called "The Wizard" or "The Magician" of hockey, also starred in India's gold-medal wins at the 1932 Los Angeles and 1936 Berlin Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• 1936 (Option 1): India won hockey gold at the Berlin Olympics, but this was not its Olympic debut in the sport.

 

• 1932 (Option 2): India won hockey gold at the Los Angeles Olympics, its second Olympic hockey appearance, not the debut.

 

• 1924 (Option 3): Hockey was not contested at the 1924 Paris Olympics, so India could not have debuted in that year.

question: A student, on his school assignment, is taking a session on how to make compost at home for using it at a park. Which fundamental duty is he performing?
option_1: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
option_2: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
option_3: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry
option_4: To protect and improve the natural environment
solution_text:
The correct answer is To protect and improve the natural environment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This corresponds to the Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(g) of the Constitution: 'to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.' (अनुच्छेद 51A(g) — प्राकृतिक पर्यावरण की रक्षा एवं सुधार)

 

• Making compost at home for use in a public park directly contributes to improving the natural environment by promoting sustainable waste management and soil health.

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties, listed under Article 51A, applicable to every citizen of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they cannot be enforced by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Article 51A(j)): 'To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity' relates to personal and collective achievement, not environmental protection.

 

• Option 2 (Article 51A(i)): 'To safeguard public property and to abjure violence' relates to protecting state/public assets and maintaining peace.

 

• Option 3 (Article 51A(h)): 'To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform' relates to rational and reformist thinking, not environmental action.

question: In August 2022, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched the ________ scheme, with an aim to provide comprehensive rehabilitation services to people engaged in begging in 75 municipalities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is SMILE-75.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In August 2022, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched the SMILE-75 Initiative (Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise), aimed at comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging across 75 municipalities/towns. (स्माइल-75 पहल — भिक्षावृत्ति में लगे व्यक्तियों का पुनर्वास)

 

• The initiative covers identification, rehabilitation, medical care/counselling, education, skill development and economic linkages for such persons.

 

• SMILE-75 is a component of the broader SMILE (Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise) umbrella scheme, which also has a sub-scheme for the welfare of transgender persons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The scheme is implemented in partnership with State/UT governments, urban local bodies and NGOs/voluntary organisations.

 

NOTE

 

• TWINKLE-75, BEAM-75 and RISE-75 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these are genuine government schemes; they are distractors not associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment's 2022 begging-rehabilitation initiative.

question: Which is the National Mission for Financial Inclusion to ensure access to financial services, namely, a basic savings and deposits accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, pension in an affordable manner?
option_2: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched on 28 August 2014, is India's National Mission for Financial Inclusion, aiming to ensure access to basic savings/deposit accounts, remittance, credit, insurance and pension in an affordable manner. (प्रधानमंत्री जन धन योजना — वित्तीय समावेशन)

 

• It provides zero-balance savings accounts along with a RuPay debit card, accidental insurance cover, and an overdraft facility for eligible account holders.

 

• PMJDY is regarded as one of the world's largest financial inclusion initiatives, having opened hundreds of millions of bank accounts, especially for previously unbanked citizens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMJDY accounts are also linked to schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) and Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) for insurance coverage.

 

NOTE

 

• Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana (Option 1): Aims at poverty alleviation through the National Rural/Urban Livelihoods Mission, not specifically financial inclusion.

 

• Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (Option 2): A rural youth skill development and placement scheme.

 

• Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (Option 3): A rural self-employment scheme (predecessor of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission), not a financial inclusion mission.

question: Which of the following plays was NOT written by Harshavardhana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikramorvasiyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vikramorvasiyam is a Sanskrit play written by the celebrated poet-dramatist Kalidasa, based on the legend of King Pururavas and the celestial nymph Urvashi; it was not written by Harshavardhana. (विक्रमोर्वशीयम् — कालिदास की रचना)

 

• Harshavardhana (7th century CE), the king of Thanesar and Kannauj, is credited with authoring three Sanskrit plays: Ratnavali, Nagananda and Priyadarshika.

 

• Harsha's court was adorned by the scholar Banabhatta, author of the Harshacharita, a biographical account of Harsha's reign.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalidasa's other major works include Abhijnanasakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha and Kumarasambhava.

 

NOTE

 

• Ratnavali (Option 2): A romantic drama genuinely authored by Harshavardhana.

 

• Nagananda (Option 3): A Buddhist-themed play genuinely authored by Harshavardhana.

 

• Priyadarshika (Option 4): A romantic comedy genuinely authored by Harshavardhana.

question: The organisms that do not have a defined nucleus or organelles are classified in to _______ Kingdom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Monera.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kingdom Monera comprises prokaryotic organisms — bacteria and cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) — which lack a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. (मोनेरा जगत — केंद्रक रहित प्रोकैरियोटिक जीव)

 

• Monera forms one of the five kingdoms in R.H. Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification (1969): Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

 

• Monerans typically have a cell wall (peptidoglycan in bacteria) and reproduce mainly through binary fission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Monera includes both eubacteria (true bacteria) and archaebacteria (which thrive in extreme environments such as hot springs and salt lakes).

 

NOTE

 

• Fungi (Option 1): Eukaryotic, mostly multicellular, heterotrophic organisms with a chitin-based cell wall; they possess a defined nucleus.

 

• Protista (Option 2): Eukaryotic, mostly unicellular organisms (e.g., Amoeba, Paramecium) that do possess a defined nucleus and organelles.

 

• Plantae (Option 4): Eukaryotic, multicellular, autotrophic organisms with a defined nucleus and organelles.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that ‘there shall be a Vice President of India’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 63.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 63 of the Constitution of India states: 'There shall be a Vice-President of India.' (अनुच्छेद 63 — भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति)

 

• The Vice-President is elected by members of an electoral college consisting of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), through proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.

 

• Under Article 64, the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and holds office for a term of five years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vice-President also acts as President when a vacancy arises due to the death, resignation or removal of the President, until a new President is elected.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 61 (Option 1): Lays down the procedure for the impeachment of the President.

 

• Article 65 (Option 3): Deals with the Vice-President acting as President or discharging the President's functions during a vacancy.

 

• Article 62 (Option 4): Deals with the time for holding elections to fill a vacancy in the office of the President and the term of office of a person elected to fill such a vacancy.

question: A javelin thrown by an athlete is in ________ motion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is curvilinear.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A javelin thrown by an athlete follows a curved trajectory under the influence of gravity, which is an example of curvilinear motion. (वक्रीय गति — भाला फेंक की गति)

 

• Curvilinear motion is motion along a curved path, as opposed to motion along a straight line.

 

• The javelin's path is a form of projectile motion, which combines uniform horizontal velocity with vertically accelerated motion due to gravity, producing a parabolic (curved) trajectory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of curvilinear motion include the motion of a ball thrown at an angle, or a vehicle turning along a curved road.

 

NOTE

 

• Oscillatory (Option 1): To-and-fro motion about a fixed mean position, such as a simple pendulum — not applicable here.

 

• Periodic (Option 2): Motion that repeats itself at regular intervals of time, such as the motion of planets — not applicable to a single javelin throw.

 

• Rectilinear (Option 3): Motion along a straight line, which does not describe the curved path of a thrown javelin.

question: The green revolution technology resulted in an increase in production of cereal production from 72.4 million tons in 1965-66 to ________ million tons in 1978-79.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 131.9.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution technology (High-Yielding Variety seeds, chemical fertilizers, irrigation and modern farm techniques) raised India's cereal production from 72.4 million tonnes in 1965-66 to 131.9 million tonnes in 1978-79. (हरित क्रांति — खाद्यान्न उत्पादन में वृद्धि)

 

• The Green Revolution in India was pioneered with the introduction of High-Yielding Variety (HYV) wheat seeds, developed with inputs from agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, drawing on Norman Borlaug's dwarf wheat varieties.

 

• States such as Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh formed the core Green Revolution belt, with wheat production registering the sharpest gains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution helped India move from a food-deficit nation reliant on imports (e.g., under PL-480) to near self-sufficiency in foodgrains by the late 1970s.

 

NOTE

 

• 150.8, 165.9 and 141.2 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these figures match the standard cited statistic for India's cereal production in 1978-79 following the Green Revolution.

question: Calculate the oxidation number of ‘S’ in H2S2O7 .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In H2S2O7 (pyrosulfuric acid/oleum), let the oxidation number of S be x. Since the compound is neutral: 2(+1) + 2(x) + 7(-2) = 0 → 2 + 2x - 14 = 0 → 2x = 12 → x = +6. (H2S2O7 में S की ऑक्सीकरण संख्या — +6)

 

• Hydrogen is taken as +1 and oxygen as -2 (standard oxidation states in this compound).

 

• H2S2O7 is formed by dissolving sulphur trioxide (SO3) in concentrated sulphuric acid (H2SO4), producing fuming sulphuric acid, commonly called oleum.

 

• This is the same +6 oxidation state that sulphur shows in ordinary sulphuric acid (H2SO4).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sulphur's oxidation state can vary widely, e.g., -2 in H2S, 0 in elemental S8, +4 in SO2, and +6 in H2SO4/H2S2O7.

 

NOTE

 

• 3, 7 and 2 (Options 1, 2 and 4): These values do not satisfy the charge-balance calculation for H2S2O7 and are therefore incorrect.

question: Which of the following is NOT an amendment made to the Airport Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) Amendment Act, 2021?
option_1: The government can call any airport a major airport just by notification.
option_2: The government will club together profit-making and loss-making airports.
option_3: The government can offer airports as a package in PPP mode to the prospective bidders.
option_4: A major airport is one which has an annual traffic of minimum 35 lakh passengers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A major airport is one which has an annual traffic of minimum 35 lakh passengers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The AERA (Amendment) Act, 2021 empowers the central government to notify any airport (or group of airports) as a 'major airport', without requiring it to individually cross a fixed passenger-traffic threshold. (AERA संशोधन अधिनियम 2021 — बड़े हवाई अड्डे की नई परिभाषा)

 

• It allows the government to club together profit-making and loss-making airports as a single group for tariff determination, so profitable airports can cross-subsidise smaller, loss-making ones.

 

• It enables the government to offer such grouped airports as a package to prospective bidders under the PPP (Public-Private Partnership) mode, similar to how the Airports Authority of India has bundled smaller airports with larger ones for privatisation.

 

• The 'minimum 35 lakh (3.5 million) annual passengers' criterion for a 'major airport' was the pre-existing definition under the original AERA Act, 2008 (as later amended in 2019) — it was not a change introduced by the 2021 Amendment; rather, the 2021 Amendment moved away from relying solely on this fixed numerical threshold.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The AERA (Airports Economic Regulatory Authority) was established under the AERA Act, 2008 to regulate tariffs and other charges for aeronautical services at major airports in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3: All represent genuine changes introduced by the AERA (Amendment) Act, 2021.

 

• Option 4: Describes the original 35-lakh-passenger threshold that predates the 2021 Amendment, making it the correct answer to this 'NOT an amendment' question.
